g.text: Formatting rules (FR-10..FR-11; samples above are real PoC output, bash-format-examples.md)
• Output = the original token sequence; only whitespace changes, and only where the bash grammar (tree-sitter-bash syntax tree) allows a newline. Nothing is re-quoted or rewritten.

• Statements one per line (";" / newline → newline, "&" kept). • A &&, ||, |, |& chain longer than 80 columns breaks AFTER the operator; the continuation is indented 2 spaces (no leading operators, no "\").
• for / while / if bodies, { … } and ( … ) indented 2; one-line loops expanded; a long for word list one word per line with "\" — the only backslashes added.
• Commands, strings, $( … ), case, functions, heredocs and their lines copied verbatim, never re-indented. • A leading cd <literal> becomes the working-dir header.
• Heredoc bodies longer than 8 lines folded into collapsible "block N" with a marker line. • Files: Changes / Reads / Runs from syntax-tree nodes only; inline interpreter
scripts listed as "inline <cmd> script, N lines — not analysed"; nothing guessed from non-bash code; lists over 3 files grouped by directory.
